items.description: Copper pipe repair – fittings, pipe section and consumables
items.rationale: Covered as necessary repair to insured pipework after escape of water (2.4.2, 2.4.3, 7.1.1(b)). Indemnity is for the actual repair, capped at a fair market rate for the materials and fittings for about 1m of copper pipe and standard fittings.

Labour for the repair is indemnified (7.1.7(g)), but only for the time reasonably required for the work described. Reference Case 16 (3 senior installer hours: t ≥ 274) and Case 7 (internal frost-burst fitting repair: t ≈ 450 for all work). Here, a day and a half with a helper is likely 10–12 hours total, so a moderate estimate is warranted.

Re-insulation of the repaired section is necessary ancillary work (7.1.7(c)), but only for the affected length. 6 pcs likely refers to 6 sleeves or meters. Reference Case 16 (connection hose: t ≈ 30). Rock wool sleeves are inexpensive; allow for installation.

One travel/call-out charge per invoice is indemnified (7.1.7(f)). Reference Case 16 (vehicle costs: t ≥ 60), but most cases with a single visit and no special circumstances are lower (Case 14: t ≈ 15).

Disposal of debris from the repair is covered (5.2.1, 7.1.7(a)), but only for the affected pipe and insulation. Reference Case 16 (auxiliary and cleaning material: t < 11), Case 13/10 (disposal lines for small loads: t ≈ 10–20). For a small amount of pipe and insulation, a moderate estimate is appropriate.
General administrative/processing fees are excluded (7.1.8(b)), as they do not constitute a repair cost and are not indemnified.

Cleaning and disinfection of the affected area is covered as necessary post-repair work (7.1.7(b)), but only for the area where water had been standing. Coating is only covered if it is necessary to restore the pre-loss standard, not as an improvement. Reference Case 12 (floor cleaning and drying: t ≈ 500 for a much larger scope). For 5 hours, a moderate estimate is warranted.
